name: The Zulu Kingdom
title: Social Hierarchy of the Zulu Kingdom: From King to Homestead
period: 1820–1879 (from Shaka's victory over Zwide to the Anglo-Zulu War)

tiers.name: The king
tiers.you: Your regiments are sworn to you alone, you decide when each of them may marry, and the shields your warriors carry belong to you; a half-brother may already be plotting your death.
tiers.kid: The Zulu king commanded the army and decided when the young warriors could marry.
tiers.rise: The throne passed by force more often than by rule: Dingane and Mhlangana murdered Shaka in 1828, Mpande overthrew Dingane with Voortrekker support, and Cetshwayo defeated his brother Mbuyazi at Ndondakusuka in 1856 and took over his father’s authority long before Mpande died in 1872.
tiers.why: Shaka, spurned as an illegitimate son of King Senzangakhona, served as a warrior under Dingiswayo of the Mthethwa, who helped him become king of the Zulu; after Dingiswayo’s death around 1816 he led the whole Mthethwa…

tiers.name: The royal kin
tiers.you: As a son of a king you have a claim to the throne and a following of your own, and every brother with a claim is a danger to you, as you are to him.
tiers.kid: The king’s brothers and sons could hope to rule one day, so they were often rivals.
tiers.rise: Birth into the royal house brought a claim to the throne and the danger that went with it: royal sons rose by winning followers and battles, and fell by murder or defeat.
tiers.why: The king’s kin were his closest rivals.

tiers.name: Izinduna, the king's officials and commanders
tiers.you: The king has made you an induna: you command a regiment, give counsel at the indaba and carry the half-moon axe of your rank, but a refused order could cost you your life.
tiers.kid: An induna was one of the king’s trusted advisers or army commanders, chosen for his leadership and bravery.
tiers.rise: The king appointed izinduna for their leadership, bravery or service and could destroy them: Ndlela, who repeatedly refused Dingane’s order to kill Mpande, was strangled for it. Mzilikazi, a general of Shaka’s, fled his service and founded a kingdom of his own.
tiers.why: An induna (plural izinduna) was a senior official appointed by the king or a chief and held in high esteem for leadership, bravery or service: an adviser, ambassador, headman or commander.

tiers.name: Chiefs of the clans
tiers.you: You head a clan that the Zulu king has drawn into his kingdom, by war or by gifts; your people still look to you, but your young men now serve in his regiments, not yours.
tiers.kid: Chiefs led the clans that joined the Zulu kingdom, but they had to obey the king.
tiers.rise: A chief held his place by birth in his lineage, but under the Zulu kings he kept it by the king’s favour. After Ulundi in 1879 most leading chiefs submitted to the British, and Wolseley shared out Zululand among thirteen chiefs, Zibhebhu among them, so that the Zulus would no longer unite under one king.
tiers.why: Before Shaka the chief of a clan lineage stood at the head of local society.

tiers.name: Warriors of the regiments
tiers.you: At twenty you are enrolled in a regiment of men your own age, with its name and shield colours; you gather at its military homestead when summoned, owe the king your loyalty and may marry only when he allows it.
tiers.kid: Young Zulu men served together in regiments of the same age and could marry only when the king allowed it.
tiers.rise: Boys from the age of six carried supplies for the army and trained as cadets until the king enlisted them. A regiment that lost a battle could return, as Cetshwayo told Rider Haggard, to find many of its wives and children beaten to death on Shaka’s orders.
tiers.why: After their twentieth birthdays young men were enrolled in a regiment (ibutho, plural amabutho), by age rather than by clan or region, and swore loyalty to the king.

tiers.name: The people of the homesteads
tiers.you: You live in a homestead of herders and farmers, keeping cattle, growing sorghum and living on milk; your sons go to the king’s regiments, and when the king decrees mourning, your fields lie unplanted.
tiers.kid: Most Zulu people lived in homesteads, herding cattle, growing sorghum and drinking milk.
tiers.rise: A man became a householder only when the king let him marry. Others left the kingdom: thousands fled into British Natal, many with their cattle, when Mpande purged those he thought dissidents in 1843.
tiers.why: Most Zulu lived in homesteads (kraals) of herders and light farmers: the Zulu relied on cattle, sorghum and milk, and milk was the basis of their diet.
